subject.title: feat(feeds): refresh followed publishers in gateway

question: Should signed ClawHub publisher following become a permanent core CLI, SQLite, and always-on gateway capability, or should the workflow be owned by a plugin with only minimal generic core seams?
rationale: The branch makes optional marketplace behavior part of core startup, storage, trust configuration, and background networking; repository policy cannot determine that product boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Route through a plugin
options.body: Pause the core stack and implement the optional follow/refresh workflow in a ClawHub plugin, adding only a narrowly proven generic core seam if the existing plugin APIs are insufficient.

options.title: Sponsor the core capability
options.body: Approve publisher feeds as a core product surface, then require a reviewed RFC contract, upgrade proof, cancellation-safe shutdown, documentation, and live behavior evidence before landing the stack.

options.title: Keep explicit CLI only
options.body: Land no automatic gateway loop and retain publisher refresh as an operator-triggered command until demand and operational behavior justify a resident service.

recommendation.title: Route through a plugin
recommendation.body: Pause the core stack and implement the optional follow/refresh workflow in a ClawHub plugin, adding only a narrowly proven generic core seam if the existing plugin APIs are insufficient.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history connects this person to the post-readiness gateway service lifecycle that would permanently own the new loop.
